name: Broken Volta
description:
Broken Volta emerged from a flooded maintenance sublevel in the Gray Zone's Ward 9 district around 2211, fronted by Ama Sørensen-Okeke (vocals, shredded guitar) alongside drummer Priya Vasquez-Lindqvist and bassist Tomás Nkemdirim-Chow. Their sound is a collision of West African highlife rhythm structures underneath Nordic black-metal distortion, with Sørensen-Okeke's voice oscillating between a keening falsetto and a raw, sub-vocal growl that chrome-enhanced listeners can feel as a second frequency layer in their cochlear implants. Politically, they pull no punches — their 2213 debut record 'Corrosion Liturgy' named three Vantablack Media executives by their registered corporate ID numbers in the bridge of the song 'Audit of Ash.'

Broken Volta's live shows are the stuff of legend and legal peril. They operate through a rotating network of encrypted mesh invites, performing in decommissioned water treatment facilities, the Gray Zone parking structures, and once, infamously, in the lobby of a defunct Tier 3 insurance tower while Meridian Security forces attempted to breach all four stairwells simultaneously. The show lasted eleven minutes before tear-dispersal drones ended it. Bootleg neural-feed recordings of that night circulate in the Gray Zone for the cost of a meal, traded like contraband scripture.
creator: Ama Sørensen-Okeke, Priya Vasquez-Lindqvist, Tomás Nkemdirim-Chow
audience: the Gray Zone residents, Ward 9 insurgent youth, labor organizers in the Circuit, contraband collectors in Tier 3
cultural_impact: Broken Volta is arguably the most politically dangerous band active in GLMZ in the 2210s. Vantablack Media's suppression attempts have paradoxically elevated them to mythic status — their name is spray-etched into the Gray Zone infrastructure from Ward 2 to Ward 14. The 'Audit of Ash' lawsuit against three executives (all quietly settled) demonstrated that a band from a flooded sublevel could make corporate legal teams sweat, and that fact has become its own kind of anthem for the Gray Zone solidarity movements.
known_fans: the Gray Zone youth gangs with political leanings
disaffected Tier 3 workers who download pirate feeds
Meridian Security informants who keep the recordings for themselves
story_hooks: A player character receives a mesh-encrypted invite to a Broken Volta show — but the location is inside a building currently under corporate surveillance for an unrelated operation, and attending means crossing two factions at once.
Tomás Nkemdirim-Chow approaches the party needing extraction: someone leaked that he's the band's bassist to a Vantablack Media asset-recovery team, and he has forty-eight hours before they find him.

A bootleg neural-feed of the infamous insurance-lobby show contains seventeen seconds of audio that wasn't part of the performance — a voice reciting what sounds like encrypted coordinates, and someone powerful wants that recording destroyed.
